meta.title: Reversing Harlow's margin decline: fix gross margin and delivery economics, not headcount
meta.subtitle: Diagnosis, recommended margin plan and first moves to reach a 3.0% operating margin by FY2028 · Board meeting, February 2027 · Prepared for Dana Whitfield, Chief Executive Officer
meta.audience: Board of directors (presented by the CEO)
meta.purpose: Approve the margin plan and its first moves

storyline.governing_thought: Fix gross margin and delivery, not headcount: seven firm levers lift margin from 1.0% to about 2.6% by FY2028, and a second wave prepared now closes the gap to 3.0%

exec_summary.text: Promotions, shrink and home delivery drove the 2.35-percentage-point fall; wages explain only 13%

sub_points.text: Gross margin and e-commerce explain 79% of the fall; productivity offset two-thirds of the wage rise
Fully costed, e-commerce loses about $10M a year, not the 6.1% margin reported

exec_summary.text: The draft 8% labor cut and e-commerce freeze would leave FY2028 margin near 1.1%, far short of 3.0%

sub_points.text: The cut saves $14.5M on paper, but lean stores run 3.1% shrink against 2.3%: we expect $4–8M back, before lost sales

exec_summary.text: Seven firm levers (about $30M) reach about 2.6%; about half of a ~$10M second wave closes the gap

sub_points.text: Gross margin $16.9M · targeted labor $5.5M · delivery $3.3M · exit 6 lease-expiry stores $4.4M (range $17–38M)
Wave 2: exit 3 more stores (board vote), cost-recovery delivery, vendor funding to 55%

exec_summary.text: Four no-regret moves in 90 days lift FY2026 income to about $25M, about $5M above the covenant

sub_points.text: Promotion reset · delivery pricing · targeted labor · notice on 6 lease-expiry stores; about $17M one-time, within $25M

exec_summary.text: Key risks are ValuMart traffic and vendor push-back; we ask the board for three decisions

sub_points.text: Endorse the plan, not the 8% cut · approve delivery repricing · prepare the 3-store vote
If wave 2 falls short, click-and-collect only reaches about 3.0% but needs the owners' consent

next_steps.action: FY2026 covenant forecast and lender briefing
Next promotion calendar without loss-making events; vendor terms
Delivery pricing live chain-wide; contract renewed. Store-by-store labor plan replacing the 8% cut
Store P&L review; notices on the 6 lease-expiry stores
Shrink pilot launched in 10 lean stores

units.text: Fix gross margin and delivery economics, not headcount: seven firm levers lift operating margin from 1.0% to ~2.6% by FY2028, and a second wave prepared now closes the gap to the 3.0% target
Reaching 3.0% by FY2028 means adding ~$35.6M of operating income (target $43.3M on pro-forma sales of $1,444M; do-nothing FY2028 $7.7M after the 2027 wage step and +3% delivery rate)

Plan constraints: margin >= 3.0% by FY2028; <= $25M one-time cost FY2026-28; operating income >= $20M in FY2026 (covenant); no closure of a store leased beyond 2027 without a board vote; keep delivery in some form

Do-nothing baseline: FY2025 ratios and scale held (optimistic), wage step on the whole labor bill (conservative), provider's +3% accepted; if erosion continued FY2026 would already breach the covenant

Hypothesis test: diagnosis holds (conditions 1-3, 6 supported; 4 partly; management's 8% cut not supported) but promotions and delivery alone (~$13M) are not enough; even all seven firm levers (~$30M) reach ~2.6%, so a second wave is needed
Gross margin (-1.02 pp) and e-commerce fulfillment (-0.84 pp) explain 79% of the 2.35 pp decline; store labor -0.30 pp = 13%; occupancy 8%; other SG&A 0%
Dollar view misleads: labor +$14.3M but sales +5.8%; at FY2023 ratio FY2025 labor would be $177.4M, so only $4.5M excess; e-commerce fulfillment $5.2M -> $18.1M

Gross-margin loss of 1.02 pp fully explained by promotion mix (-0.70 pp, -$10.5M) and shrink (-0.50 pp, -$7.5M); private label +0.18 pp (+$2.7M) offset less than a fifth; vendor funding 55% -> 46%; shrink $39.1M (waste 45%, theft 35%, admin 20%)

Deeper promotion has not paid for itself: 38% of events lose money; +5 pp promo share costs $10.5M a year and needs ~$53M of new sales; category team's 'promotions work' fails its own arithmetic (break-even 2.3 pp of extra share; correlation)

Promotion implication: cut loss-making events chain-wide, require vendor funding per event, keep targeted depth only in ValuMart-exposed stores while traffic is measured, move the value message to private label; stage and track the reset because the needed promotion level is an open question

Productivity absorbed two-thirds of the 9.4% wage rise (wage +1.11 pp, productivity -0.77 pp); lean-labor stores run more shrink (Q1 3.1% vs Q4 2.3%); rebalance hours rather than cut them (waste and receiving errors 65% of shrink)

Fully costed, e-commerce loses ~$10.4M a year, not +6.1%: delivered order -$12.34, click-and-collect -$1.64; delivery -$9.5M; break-even needs 94% (delivery) / 39% (C&C) of sales new vs 30% survey; freezing locks in the loss

Management draft plan (8% hours cut + e-commerce freeze) leaves FY2028 margin ~1.1% ($16.6M): added shrink $3.8-7.5M (midpoint $5.6M), each 1% of sales lost ~ $3.0M, freeze keeps -$10.4M, promotions untouched, shrink effects lag the covenant

Three options: A draft (reject), B margin-first (recommend: ~2.6% firm, ~3.4% with full second wave, ~$17M one-time, ~$25M FY2026), C click-and-collect only (~3.0% on firm levers, $42.9M; breaks delivery commitment; fallback if second-wave delivery pricing fails); deeper promotions also rejected (~$2.1M per point)

Seven firm levers worth ~$30.1M (range $16.8-38.0M) by FY2028: promotion reset 6.1, vendor funding 3.7, private label 4.3, shrink 2.8, targeted labor 5.5, delivery pricing 3.3, exit 6 stores 4.4; with sizing, evidence strength and start

Tested delivery pricing adds ~$2.5M a year (+$0.8M contract), keeps the service; delivered orders still lose ~$9.04 (~$6.4M a year), only a quarter of the loss fixed; next test cost-recovery pricing or membership (~$3M)

Exit the six loss-making stores whose leases end by 2027 (~$4.4M a year, no board vote, payback < 1 year); other three take ~3.4 years and $7.5M (44% of one-time budget): test a fix for 6 months, board vote mid-FY2027 if it fails; pro-rata split is the main uncertainty (~$3M)

Firm levers take margin to ~2.6% ($37.8M) by FY2028; gap $5-6M; second wave ~$9.9M (exit 3 stores 2.2, cost-recovery delivery 3.0, vendor funding to 55% 4.7), about half needed; full plan 3.4%; prepare all three now

Four no-regret first moves in 90 days (promotion reset with vendor terms, delivery pricing roll-out, targeted labor rebalancing, notice on 6 stores) lift FY2026 operating income to ~$24.9M, ~$5M above covenant; why these first; FY2027-28 roadmap
Mid-FY2027 checkpoint: if run-rate margin is below ~2.4%, trigger the second wave in full and put fallback C to the owners
If about a third of FY2025's $18M erosion recurs, the FY2026 covenant headroom is gone: track monthly and brief the lender early
One-time cost ~$17M inside the $25M cap with ~$8M contingency; firm wave alone ~$9.5M; cap holds unless allowances prove ~80% too low; only the $7.5M lease exit is from the pack

Sensitivities with triggers and responses: traffic (-$2.0M), vendor funding stays 46% (-$3.7M), 50% new e-commerce (loss -$5.3M; delivery still -$8.50/order), shrink only 2.45% (-$2.1M), wage +6% (-$3.6M), loss split (-$1.4M), FY2026 erosion (~$5M slippage); diagnosis robust
Gates: comps in ValuMart areas below -4.2%; vendor funding share in next two cycles; shrink pilot scale only if >= 0.2 pp gain; store P&Ls before notice; monthly operating income vs $20M path

Three decisions today: endorse the margin-first plan in place of the 8% cut; approve delivery repricing roll-out and e-commerce guardrail; authorize preparation of the second wave (3-store vote by mid-FY2027, cost-recovery pilot, vendor terms)

Next 90 days: covenant forecast and lender briefing (CFO, wk 2); promotion calendar and vendor terms (Category, wk 4); delivery pricing live and contract (E-commerce, wk 6); labor plan (COO, wk 6); store P&L and notices (Property/CFO, wk 8); shrink pilot in 10 stores (COO, wk 12)

Quarterly scorecard: promo share 29% -> 25%; vendor funding 46% -> 50%+; private label 18.5% -> 21%; shrink 2.6% -> 2.3%; loss per delivered order $12.34 -> < $5; operating income >= $20M FY2026, 3.0% FY2028
Key risks are ValuMart traffic and vendor push-back; if wave 2 falls short, click-and-collect-only reaches ~3.0% but needs owners' consent
Appendix A1: ratio changes sum to the 2.35 pp decline; mix and labor decompositions reconcile
Appendix A2: e-commerce fulfillment rebuilds exactly from order data; fully costed loss -2.6, -6.0, -10.4; team's 6.1% less delivery = -0.4% before cannibalization
Appendix A3: low case ~$16.8M (FY2028 1.7%), base $30.1M (2.6%), high $38.0M (3.2%); FY2026 in-year $9.6M
Appendix A4: choices made without CEO input (fiscal timing, baseline, wage step, pro-rata split), claims not relied on, team estimates, data caveats
